question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{50}$ be a random sample of size $n=50$ from a population with probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{{x}^{6}}, & x\ge 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.1,$ calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}<1.2).$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.2\,$ | $\,0.1131\,$ | $\,0.1112\,$ | $\,0.1093\,$ |
| $\,-1.1\,$ | $\,0.1335\,$ | $\,0.1314\,$ | $\,0.1292\,$ |
| $\,-1.0\,$ | $\,0.1562\,$ | $\,0.1539\,$ | $\,0.1515\,$ |
